entry.label: Viability
entry.description: Viability is not short-term survival or financial solvency. It concerns whether a system can keep producing itself as a coherent actor while its environment and internal conditions change.
entry.canonical_definition: The capacity of a system to continue as a recognisable whole by balancing present operations, regulation, learning, adaptation and identity under changing conditions.

profile.title: Viability
profile.canonical_definition: The capacity of a system to continue as a recognisable whole by balancing present operations, regulation, learning, adaptation and identity under changing conditions.
profile.summary: Viability is not short-term survival or financial solvency. It concerns whether a system can keep producing itself as a coherent actor while its environment and internal conditions change.
profile.why_it_matters: A viable organisation must handle today's work, disturbances and accountability while sensing and preparing for tomorrow. Central control cannot substitute for local regulatory capacity.
practice_connections: protect local autonomy while maintaining cohesion
separate current operations from future intelligence
test whether identity can change intelligently
common_misreadings: viability means survival of the fittest
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public management-cybernetics, systems-practice and evolutionary-theory sources. Distinct theoretical traditions are not collapsed into one consensus account.
